claims_extracted: The Stage-0 source record cites a Federal Reserve note stating that order-flow imbalances can amplify price movements in Treasury markets.
The Stage-0 hypothesis explicitly maps the mechanism to liquid FTMO instruments using M15-H1 tick-volume or signed-volume proxies while marking MT5 equivalence as unverified.
The new repo implementation uses signed EURUSD M15 tick volume, volume/volatility filters, and bounded time exits; it is not London breakout/sweep, BB squeeze, simple trend, or RSI mean reversion.
EURUSD appears in the FTMO terminal universe evidence; this screening remains research-only until MT5 data equivalence is separately proven.
limitations: The external mechanism source is Treasury-market evidence, not direct EURUSD broker evidence.
MT5 tick volume is a noisy proxy for directional order flow and may not represent real traded volume.
The current CSV is research data; terminal-derived MT5 equivalence is not assumed.
This is a one-shot Phase 8D screen and not a parameter-tuning continuation of prior failed candidates.
disconfirming_relevance: The signed-volume proxy can be dominated by candle construction noise rather than true order flow.
Spread/slippage can erase any continuation after high-imbalance bars.
The mechanism may be too short-lived for M15 bars.
